question: How many ATAC-seq peaks are significant caQTLs at 10% FDR using the Benjamini–Hochberg q-value reported by RASQUAL?

nodes.label: Confirm that the RASQUAL BH q-value column corresponds to peak-level multiple-testing correction
Decide on the FDR significance threshold and any inclusions or exclusions of peaks
Filter ATAC-seq peaks whose RASQUAL BH q-values are below or equal to the 10% FDR threshold
Count the number of peaks passing the 10% FDR threshold to obtain the total significant caQTL peaks

Load RASQUAL caQTL summary statistics table and verify that the BH q-value column is defined at the peak level (e.g. by checking documentation or column description and confirming one q-value per peak)

Set the FDR significance threshold to q <= 0.10 and, if needed, subset the table to the relevant set of ATAC-seq peaks (e.g. autosomes only or primary peak list) without applying any additional statistical filters
Filter the RASQUAL caQTL summary table to retain only rows corresponding to ATAC-seq peaks whose BH q-value column is not missing and is less than or equal to 0.10
Count the number of unique ATAC-seq peak identifiers in the filtered table as the total number of significant caQTL peaks at 10% FDR
